lessons.title: Data Factory vs. SSIS vs. Fabric Data Factory

slots.practicalActivity: Read through the Azure Data Factory overview blade in the Azure portal (or the Fabric trial's Data Factory workload), and write a one-paragraph comparison of ETL vs. ELT and ADF vs. SSIS vs. Fabric Data Factory, naming a concrete scenario you've encountered or can imagine (a nightly batch load, a legacy SSIS migration, a Fabric-first shop) where each tool choice would win.
slots.deliverable: A short written comparison note covering ETL vs. ELT and ADF vs. SSIS vs. Fabric Data Factory, each tied to a specific scenario.

slots.practicalActivity: In the Azure portal, create a real Azure Data Factory V2 instance (or reuse an existing dev factory), following the four creation decisions — resource group, region, globally-unique name, and V2 version — then select Launch studio and tour all four Studio home-page tiles: Ingest, Orchestrate, Transform data, Configure SSIS.
slots.deliverable: A running Azure Data Factory V2 instance, with a short note recording its exact globally-unique name and what each of the four Studio home-page tiles is for.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Manage hub in your new factory and locate where linked services, triggers, and integration runtimes will live in later chapters. Write a one-page "factory tour" note in your own words explaining the difference between the factory's Azure Resource Manager overview page (in the Azure portal) and Data Factory Studio itself.
slots.deliverable: A one-page written factory-tour note distinguishing the Azure portal's resource view from Data Factory Studio, plus a bullet list of the 4 Studio tiles and what each is for.

lessons.title: Connecting to Azure SQL & On-Premises SQL Server

slots.practicalActivity: Create two real linked services in your factory: an Azure Blob Storage linked service (test both Account key and a managed identity authentication method) and a SQL Server linked service pointing at a real AdventureWorksDW2014 or Northwind database, testing the connection on each before selecting Create.
slots.deliverable: Two working, test-passed linked services (Azure Blob Storage and SQL Server) visible in the Manage hub.

slots.practicalActivity: Build two datasets on top of the previous slot's linked services — a CSV dataset on Blob Storage and a SQL table dataset against AdventureWorksDW2014 — then parameterize the Blob Storage linked service (for account/container name) and the SQL dataset (for table name) so the same dataset definition can point at different tables at runtime.
slots.deliverable: Two parameterized datasets, each successfully checked with Preview data, with their linked-service/dataset parameters visible in the dataset's Parameters tab.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a third linked service (a second SQL database, or a Northwind connection if AdventureWorksDW2014 was your first) and a dataset on top of it, then write a short note comparing how parameterizing a linked service differs from parameterizing a dataset, using your 3 real linked services as concrete examples.
slots.deliverable: A third working linked service and dataset pair, plus a short written note contrasting linked-service vs. dataset parameterization.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a new pipeline with a single Copy activity that copies a real table from your AdventureWorksDW2014 SQL linked service into the Blob Storage container as CSV. Use the column mapping UI to deliberately rename at least 2 output columns, and turn on schema drift to confirm the pipeline tolerates an extra source column.
slots.deliverable: A working Copy-activity pipeline with explicit column mapping (2+ renamed columns) and schema drift enabled, run successfully in Debug mode.

lessons.title: Web, Wait, Fail & Set Variable Activities

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Lookup activity that reads a table name from a small configuration table, a Set Variable activity that stores the result, and a Stored Procedure activity that logs a "run started" row back to SQL Server. Add a Wait activity and a Fail activity wired to run only if the Copy activity from the previous slot fails.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline containing Lookup, Set Variable, Stored Procedure, Wait, and Fail activities, run in Debug mode with every activity's status checked.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the exact 3-activity chain this lesson teaches — Lookup, Copy, Stored Procedure — against your real AdventureWorksDW2014/Blob Storage connections, wiring Copy to Stored Procedure on the Succeeded dependency condition and Copy to a Fail activity on Failed, then run the whole pipeline in Debug mode and confirm each activity's status.
slots.deliverable: A working end-to-end pipeline (Lookup, Copy, Stored Procedure, with a Fail branch) with a successful Debug run showing all expected activity statuses.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Pipelines & Activities: without reusing the previous slot's exact pipeline, design and build an original second pipeline from scratch — copying a different AdventureWorksDW2014 or Northwind table, with its own Lookup/Copy/Fail chain and a different combination of dependency conditions — documenting your activity choices in comments on the pipeline canvas.
slots.deliverable: One original pipeline you designed yourself (not copied from the lesson), run successfully in Debug mode, with a short written note explaining the dependency conditions you chose and why.

slots.practicalActivity: Add pipeline-level parameters and variables to your Chapter 3 pipeline, wrap part of it in an If Condition activity that branches based on a parameter value, and add a ForEach activity that loops over an array of table names, running the Copy activity once per table inside the loop.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline using parameters, variables, an If Condition branch, and a ForEach loop that copies multiple tables in a single run.

slots.practicalActivity: Add an Until activity that polls a condition (e.g. waits until a Lookup returns a specific status value), and an Execute Pipeline activity that calls your Chapter 3 pipeline as a child pipeline, passing parameters into it using Data Factory expression language (@pipeline().parameters, @activity() outputs, @pipeline().RunId).
slots.deliverable: A parent pipeline using Until and Execute Pipeline, successfully passing expression-built parameter values into the child pipeline.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine this chapter's pieces into one original orchestration pipeline: a ForEach loop over a list of tables, an If Condition inside the loop that uses Switch to route small vs. large tables to different Copy activity settings, and the system variable @pipeline().RunId logged via a Stored Procedure activity.
slots.deliverable: One original control-flow pipeline combining ForEach, an If Condition/Switch branch, and a logged system variable, run successfully in Debug mode.

lessons.title: What Is a Mapping Data Flow?

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new mapping data flow, turn on Data Flow debug mode, add a Source pointing at your AdventureWorksDW2014 FactInternetSales (or Northwind Order Details) table and a Sink writing to a new Blob Storage/ADLS Gen2 container, and use the Inspect and Data Preview tabs to confirm the column metadata and sample rows at each stage.
slots.deliverable: A working data flow with one Source and one Sink, debugged with Data Preview showing real rows flowing through it.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the data flow with a Filter (exclude cancelled or zero-value orders), a Derived Column (compute a line-total or margin field), a Join to a dimension table (e.g. DimProduct or DimCustomer), an Aggregate (totals by category), and a Conditional Split routing high-value vs. low-value rows to two different sinks.
slots.deliverable: One data flow chaining Filter, Derived Column, Join, Aggregate, and Conditional Split, verified row-by-row using Data Preview.

slots.practicalActivity: Open your data flow's debug cluster settings, experiment with partitioning options on the Optimize tab for the Join and Aggregate transformations, and compare the Spark execution time shown in the data flow's run details before and after adjusting the partitioning scheme.
slots.deliverable: A before/after performance comparison (execution time and partition count) for your data flow, with a written note on exactly what you changed.

slots.practicalActivity: Design an original mapping data flow from scratch against a different AdventureWorksDW2014 or Northwind table pairing than the lesson examples — your own choice of filter condition, join, and aggregate logic — answering a specific business question you write down first, such as "total sales by region and quarter."
slots.deliverable: One original data flow answering a business question you defined yourself, with its sink output verified in Data Preview.

slots.practicalActivity: Operationalize the previous slot's data flow inside a pipeline using a Data Flow activity, parameterize at least one data flow parameter (e.g. a date filter) from the pipeline, and run the whole pipeline in Debug mode twice with two different parameter values to confirm the parameterized data flow executes correctly end to end.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline with a parameterized Data Flow activity, run successfully in Debug mode with the parameter value changed between two runs.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Schedule trigger (e.g. daily at a specific time) and attach it to one of your existing pipelines, then create a Tumbling Window trigger on a different pipeline with a defined window size, inspecting the system variables (@trigger().outputs.windowStartTime / windowEndTime) available inside that pipeline.
slots.deliverable: Two real triggers — one Schedule, one Tumbling Window — attached to pipelines and published, with the Tumbling Window's window-time system variables referenced inside its pipeline.

slots.practicalActivity: Create an Event-based (Storage event) trigger that fires when a new blob lands in your Chapter 2 storage container, then set up a trigger dependency so a second pipeline's trigger only fires after the first pipeline's trigger run succeeds.
slots.deliverable: One Event-based trigger that fires on a real file upload, and one chained trigger dependency between two pipelines.

slots.practicalActivity: Upload a test file to your storage container to fire the Event trigger, watch the chained dependent trigger fire the second pipeline from the Monitor hub, and write a short incident-style note describing the exact order of trigger firings you observed.
slots.deliverable: A Monitor-hub log sequence showing the Event trigger firing and the dependent trigger following it, plus a short written trigger-timeline note.

slots.practicalActivity: In the Manage hub, inspect the default Azure Integration Runtime attached to your factory, note its region and which activities currently use it, then explicitly set one Copy activity to reference the Azure IR with a different region to observe the cross-region data movement warning.
slots.deliverable: A written note identifying your factory's default Azure IR and its region, plus a screenshot or note of the cross-region warning triggered deliberately.

slots.practicalActivity: If you have a local SQL Server available (e.g. the AdventureWorks2012 instance from the T-SQL course), install and register a Self-Hosted Integration Runtime, create a linked service that uses it, and run a test Copy activity pulling from that on-premises-style source into Blob Storage. Otherwise, document the exact installation and registration steps using the factory's provided authentication key.
slots.deliverable: Either a working Self-Hosted IR with a successful on-premises Copy activity, or a detailed written installation/registration runbook if no local SQL Server is available.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Monitor hub and review the run history for every pipeline you've built so far, filtering by status and date range. Then configure an Alert rule that fires on pipeline failure, and set a non-default retry policy (count and interval) on your Chapter 3 Copy activity.
slots.deliverable: A filtered Monitor-hub view of your pipeline run history, plus one configured Alert rule and one Copy activity with a customized retry policy.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately break one pipeline (e.g. point a Copy activity at a nonexistent table) to trigger a real failure, handle it with a dependency-condition error-handling branch, and configure diagnostic settings to send pipeline run logs to a Log Analytics workspace, then write a simple KQL query that returns the failed run's log entry.
slots.deliverable: One deliberately-triggered pipeline failure handled by an error-handling branch, plus a KQL query against Log Analytics returning that failed run's log entry.

lessons.title: Dataflow Gen2 vs. Mapping Data Flows

slots.practicalActivity: In a Microsoft Fabric workspace (trial capacity is fine), create a Fabric Data Factory pipeline and a Dataflow Gen2, comparing the Dataflow Gen2 authoring experience (Power Query-based) directly against the ADF mapping data flow you built in Chapter 5 for similar transformation logic.
slots.deliverable: One Fabric pipeline and one Dataflow Gen2, plus a written side-by-side comparison of Dataflow Gen2 vs. your Chapter 5 mapping data flow.

lessons.title: When to Choose ADF vs. Fabric

slots.practicalActivity: Configure your Dataflow Gen2 (or a Fabric pipeline Copy activity) to write its output into a OneLake lakehouse table, then take one of your Chapter 3 ADF pipelines and manually recreate its logic as a Fabric pipeline, documenting every setting that changed in the move.
slots.deliverable: Data landed in a OneLake lakehouse table from Fabric, plus a migrated Fabric-pipeline version of one Chapter 3 ADF pipeline with a written list of what changed.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page decision memo recommending ADF vs. Fabric Data Factory for two different hypothetical scenarios — a company already deep in Power BI/Fabric, and one with heavy existing SSIS/on-premises investment — grounded in the OneLake and migration work from the previous slot.
slots.deliverable: A one-page ADF-vs-Fabric decision memo covering two concrete scenarios.

slots.practicalActivity: Reconfigure your Blob Storage and SQL linked services to authenticate with the factory's system-assigned managed identity instead of account keys or passwords, store any remaining secret in Azure Key Vault and reference it via a Key Vault-backed linked service, assign an appropriate RBAC role, and connect your factory to a Git repository (Azure DevOps or GitHub) for source control.
slots.deliverable: Linked services authenticating via managed identity (no plaintext secrets), one Key Vault-referenced secret, and a Git-connected factory with your pipelines committed to a feature branch.

slots.practicalActivity: Publish your Git-connected factory's collaboration branch to the live ADF service, then export its ARM template from the Manage hub and inspect the exported JSON to identify which parameters would need different values across Dev/Test/Prod environments.
slots.deliverable: A successfully published factory, plus an exported ARM template with at least 3 environment-specific parameters identified in writing.

slots.practicalActivity: Working through the Northwind Retail scenario, translate its 4-sentence stakeholder ask into your own requirements table (business language to technical requirement to course concept), and sketch the 5-stage end-to-end architecture diagram, exactly as the lesson demonstrates, before writing any pipeline.
slots.deliverable: A written requirements-traceability table and an end-to-end architecture sketch for the Northwind Retail capstone.

lessons.title: Capstone: Connect & Build the Copy Pipeline

slots.practicalActivity: Build the capstone's first real stage: connect to the on-premises-style SQL Server source (via Self-Hosted IR if available, or your existing SQL linked service) and build a Copy activity that reliably lands raw Northwind/AdventureWorksDW2014 sales data into a raw-zone storage container in Parquet format.
slots.deliverable: A working Copy activity landing real sales data as Parquet in a raw-zone storage container.

lessons.title: Capstone: Add Control Flow & Error Handling

slots.practicalActivity: Add control flow around the capstone's Copy activity so it handles a missing source table or a transient connection failure without losing data: a Lookup to check the source exists first, a retry policy on the Copy, and a Fail/alert branch on Failed. Test each failure path by deliberately breaking the source.
slots.deliverable: A capstone pipeline that survives a deliberately-triggered missing-table or connection failure without silent data loss, verified by actually testing the failure path.

lessons.title: Capstone: Build the Mapping Data Flow

slots.practicalActivity: Build the capstone's mapping data flow: filter out invalid or cancelled orders, join to region and product-category dimension tables, aggregate total sales by region and category, and sink the result into an Azure SQL Database curated table, verifying the aggregated numbers against a manual spot-check.
slots.deliverable: A working capstone mapping data flow producing a verified, correctly-aggregated region-by-category sales table in Azure SQL Database.

slots.practicalActivity: Attach a Schedule trigger so the whole capstone pipeline runs unattended before an 8 AM deadline, switch all its linked services to managed identity authentication, and configure an Alert rule plus Log Analytics logging so a 3 AM failure would be observable without anyone watching the Monitor hub live.
slots.deliverable: A scheduled, managed-identity-secured, monitored capstone pipeline with one configured Alert rule and Log Analytics logging in place.

slots.practicalActivity: Record yourself (or write a structured walkthrough script) explaining the finished capstone pipeline end to end, in under five minutes, to someone who has never seen it — the architecture, each stage's purpose, and exactly how it satisfies all 4 original stakeholder requirements from the Business Requirements lesson's traceability table.
slots.deliverable: A 5-minute capstone walkthrough (recorded or scripted) that explicitly maps back to each of the 4 original stakeholder requirements.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can design, build, secure, and monitor real Azure Data Factory and Fabric Data Factory pipelines — linked services, Copy activities, control flow, mapping data flows, triggers, integration runtimes, and CI/CD — and has shipped one complete capstone pipeline moving on-premises SQL Server data into a scheduled, secured, monitored curated table.
